title: Trustworthy inference launch guide and SLO ops sprint plan
content:
Overview:
This doc is a working guide for the operations sprint that will prepare the inference stack for a cross-functional product launch with hard SLO commitments. Objective is to create an actionable 90-day plan (three 2-week sprints + stabilization) that teams (serving runtime, infra, product, SRE, developer-experience, and solutions eng) can follow to move from pre-launch to a reliable GA with clear rollback, escalation, and monitoring patterns.

Why this exists (context):
- The product team plans to publish a new hosted inference route for a high-volume feature in Q3. We need a reproducible ops runway (telemetry, synthetic tests, canary policy, capacity safety) and agreed SLOs before enabling GA.
- Past launches exposed gaps: missing prefix-cache visibility, brittle autoscaling on long-tail bursts, and unclear owner for quality regressions tied to model upgrades.

Scope (what's in/out):
In scope:
- Establish SLO definitions for latency, error rate, availability, and model-quality regressions for the new route.
- Instrumentation and dashboards for token-level latency, inference queue depth, model variant rollout impacts, and prefix-KV cache hit-rate.
- Canary + progressive rollout policy and rollback playbook.
- Runbooks and oncall assignment for launch window + first 30 days.
- Load tests and chaos experiments (eg. GPU node preemption, network partitions) executed in staging.
Out of scope:
- Major runtime refactors (unless critical blocker surfaced by tests).
- Customer-specific contractual SLA negotiations (handled separately by GTM/legal).

Success criteria (acceptance):
- Defined SLOs with thresholds and measurement windows documented and approved by SRE, product and serving-runtime leads.
- Dashboards and alerting configured: P95 latency, error-rate, availability, cache-hit rate; alerts with runbooks.
- Canary completed with zero-suppressed regressions for quality and performance for 7 days at canary traffic level.
- Load tests show autoscaling keeps P95 latency under SLO at target traffic + 30% headroom.
- Oncall rotations assigned and escalation lists published.

Proposed SLOs (initial draft — for review):
- Availability: 99.95% per 30-day window for the inference route (measured as successful HTTP 2xx responses excluding user-aborted requests).
- Latency: P95 tail <= 450ms for short-context requests (<=256 tokens) and P95 <= 1.2s for long-context (>=1024 tokens), 30-day window.
- Error rate: client-visible 5xx + 4xx-excluding-rate-limit <= 0.15% per day.
- Model-quality: regression detection — no more than 1% drop in normalized BLEU/semantic-similarity on canonical prompt-set over a 14-day rolling window when compared to baseline. (Metric and baseline definition owned by applied-ml + product)
Notes on measurement:
- Use tokenized-duration telemetry from serving-runtime to compute per-token latency breakdown.
- Model-quality requires evaluation harness (product-owned prompt set + applied-ml scoring pipeline).

Key stakeholders and owners:
- Product (route owner): Aparna Rao — defines feature acceptance and quality bar.
- Serving runtime lead: Diego Martínez — kernel selection, cache visibility, perf counters.
- SRE lead: Jordan Lee — alerting, runbooks, oncall choreography.
- Applied ML: Hannah Kim — evaluation harness, model validation.
- Developer Experience: Eliot Turner — SDK compatibility, consumer SDK rollout notes.
- Solutions Eng (customer readiness): Priya Gupta (advisory)

90-day sprint plan (high-level):
- Sprint 0 (preparation, 2 weeks):
  - Finalize SLO targets and ownership matrix.
  - Inventory telemetry gaps (list events/metrics missing).
  - Create canary config (traffic percentage, model variants, region routing).
  - Draft alerts and runbooks (initial versions).
  - Prep load-test harness and synthetic prompt set.
- Sprint 1 (hardening observability, 2 weeks):
  - Implement missing telemetry: KV cache hit/miss, batching stats, per-request model-variant tag.
  - Dashboards: P95/P99 latency by model variant, queue depth, batch size distribution.
  - Alerts: latency burn, error spikes, autoscaler saturation.
  - Execute canary dry-run in staging (0% prod traffic).
- Sprint 2 (canary, load test, ops playbooks, 2 weeks):
  - Run canary in prod at 5% traffic for 72h. Monitor regressions.
  - Run load tests to target +30% headroom; iterate autoscaler policies.
  - Run chaos experiments in staging (node GPU preemption, sim latency spikes) and capture fallout.
  - Finalize runbooks and communication templates.
- Sprint 3 (progressive rollout + stabilization, 2 weeks):
  - Progressive rollout to 25% -> 50% -> 100% as long as canary checks pass.
  - Keep enhanced monitoring and extra oncall coverage during ramp.
  - Capture telemetry and model-quality evals; sign-off to GA.
- Post-launch (30 days ops runway):
  - Daily health report for first 7 days, then every-other-day until day 30.
  - Postmortem cadence: immediate for Sev2+, weekly roll-ups for lower-level anomalies.

Milestones and decision gates:
- Gate 1 (end of Sprint 0): SLOs agreed and telemetry gaps triaged. Decision: proceed to instrument.
- Gate 2 (end of Sprint 1): Dashboards + alerts live in prod; canary config validated in staging. Decision: permit small-volume canary.
- Gate 3 (end of Sprint 2): Canary OK + load tests pass. Decision: progressive rollout enabled.
- Gate 4 (end of Sprint 3): GA sign-off; oncall and runbooks in place.

Runbooks (high level excerpts):
- High latency P95 > SLO:
  1) Pager to SRE oncall -> SRE Triage: check autoscaler metrics, queue depth, batch size histogram.
  2) If queue depth high and GPU utilization low -> possible batching regression or eviction: page serving-runtime lead.
  3) If GPU utilization at peak and latency high -> evaluate scaling (temporarily increase reserved capacity or activate burst capacity).
  4) If model variant correlates with latency spike -> rollback to previous variant via rollout service.
- Model-quality regression detected:
  1) Notify applied-ml and product. Pause new rollouts if in-progress.
  2) Run evaluation harness on warm-run traffic samples.
  3) If confirmed, trigger immediate rollback and customer comms plan.

Escalation contacts (primary/secondary):
- SRE lead: Jordan Lee / backup: Carla Nguyen
- Serving runtime: Diego Martínez / backup: Rajesh Patel
- Applied ML: Hannah Kim / backup: Lian Zhao
- Product manager: Aparna Rao / backup: Samir Verma

Telemetry checklist (must-have events/metrics):
- request.duration.total (ms) with token counts and model_variant tag
- request.step.decode (ms), request.step.kernel (ms) - breakdowns
- batch.size distribution and per-worker queue depth
- kvcache.hit/miss rates + key TTL evictions
- model.evals.quality.score for canonical prompts (daily)
- infra.node.gpu.utilization, infra.node.preemptions
- autoscaler.desired/actual replicas and scaling actions

Load-test plan (minimal):
- Baseline synthetic profile: 60% short-context, 30% medium, 10% long-context; match expected client mix.
- Target traffic scenarios: 1x (expected peak), 1.3x (headroom), 3x (stress). Measure P95/P99 and error rates.
- Spike test: 10x burst for 2 minutes to validate request throttling and graceful degradation.

Communication plan and cadence:
- Weekly sync (thurs 11am PT) during sprints with short pre-read (SRE + runtime + product). Invite list: SRE, serving-runtime, applied-ml, product, developer-experience, solutions-eng.
- Canary daily stand-up for 5 days during rollout (15m) with a short health summary in #ops-launch channel.
- Exec readiness update at Gate 3 with a one-pager and risk summary.

Risk register (top risks):
- Risk: Model-quality regression not detected quickly -> Mitigation: daily automated evals + human-in-the-loop checks for first 14 days.
- Risk: Autoscaler slow to react for sudden long-context traffic -> Mitigation: conservative headroom, reactive manual scaling runbook, pre-warmed pool for long-context heavy routes.
- Risk: Cache poisoning or eviction pattern -> Mitigation: enhanced cache metrics, per-customer cache quotas, circuit-breaker for cache-miss storms.

Open questions / items for discussion:
- Should GA SLO availability target be 99.95% or 99.9% for this route? Product prefers 99.95 but infra cost impact needs sizing. (action: infra to provide cost delta for 99.95 vs 99.9 by EOD 2026-05-19)
- How to handle multi-region fallbacks for model variants that are region-specific? Need policy for cross-region routing and data residency constraints.
- What is the canonical prompt set for model-quality evals? Product + applied-ml to finalize by next week.

Notes to self (working reminders):
- Add an entry in infra runbooks about reserving burst capacity via dedicated pool for launch days.
- Coordinate with Console team to surface route-level SLOs in the product dashboard. (Eliot)
- Make sure SDK change log has a note about canary behavior and expected error codes during ramp.

Next steps (this week):
- Sprint 0 kickoff meeting (Jordan) — schedule and invite core group.
- Diego to share telemetry inventory and quick-win list to close gaps in 48h.
- Hannah to share eval harness link and sample output format.
- Aparna to confirm the final product acceptance checklist by 2026-05-18.

Appendix (quick links):
- Staging canary runbook: confluence:INF-CANARY-7
- Load-test harness repo: git:github.com/redwood-inference/load-tests
- Eval pipeline notebook: confluence:INF-EVAL-11

End of doc. This is a living doc — expect iterative edits.
